coffee and etan (frankincense) smoke; loud chatter of me and my siblings; we talk about school, tests, university applications, work; popcorn, sometimes kolo; three rounds: abol, tona, baraka.
Visual world: our home in Addis on a Sunday morning, warm light, a staircase, a room with fresh grass on the floor, small cups, a jebena on coals, rising smoke. Warm painterly illustration. No real faces: people seen from behind, in silhouette, or as hands. Subject centred. No text in images.
Shots and lines (use the lines verbatim, one shot each):
1. Upstairs bedroom, morning light, door ajar (hook) | MOM: "Nolawi! Delina! Come down here!" | NARRATOR: "Every Sunday morning, it starts the same way: my mom's voice, from downstairs."
2. Feet coming down the staircase (leaving the week behind) | "Whatever the week was, we come down."
3. Housekeeper's hands washing green coffee beans (ritual already begun) | "Downstairs, the coffee has already begun."
4. Beans roasting in a pan, smoke rising toward the stairs (smell as invitation) | "The beans crackle in the pan, and the smell climbs the stairs before we do."
5. Jebena on coals, etan smoke curling (time slows) | "Etan smoke curls through the room. Nobody is in a hurry."
6. Bowl of popcorn and kolo on the grass (homely detail) | "There's popcorn, sometimes kolo, and a lot of noise."
7. Family seated, seen from behind, first pour (together) | "With the first cup, abol, we catch up on the week: school, tests, work."
8. Two siblings' silhouettes laughing and gesturing (chatter) | "With the second, tona, it's university applications, and everyone has an opinion."
9. Slow third pour, softer light (blessing) | "The third cup is baraka, the blessing. The room gets quieter."
10. Empty cups, smoke fading (moment passing) | "The coffee was never really the point."
11. The house from outside, late-morning light (why it matters) | "It's the one hour every week we're all in the same room. Next Sunday, she'll call again, and we'll come down."
